attributes.summary: Audit-before-acceptance round 1: delegated via clink/codex (exfu-auditor, read-only, gpt-5.6-sol), 1 round, return salvage needed. Verdict: revise — 2 high (redaction seam contradicted T1 theme boundary; role-model HITL reopened T1's toy-is-a-template ruling), 4 medium (survey contract too vague to bind a T3, primitives partition overclaimed, numeric domain unruled, honesty signals undefined), 1 low (no version metadata on results). Full return: .exfu/returns/t2-engine-audit-r1.json.

Draft revised addressing all 7 findings: engine results declared trusted-internal with field classification and a no-deal disclosure contract (data-layer alone builds role-safe payloads); role model bound to two directional roles with T1-amendment escalation path; normative survey algorithm contract added (curve construction, interpolation, interval/no-crossing states, per-respondent validation, edge-case vectors); primitives partitioned engine-wide/toolkit/inflection-specific with a consumption map; numeric domain fixed (finite, positive, one currency, zero-width defined); honesty signals given versioned definitions; version metadata required on every result. HITL now Q1 tolerance semantics, Q2 money representation, Q3 small-sample threshold. Status remains draft — awaiting operator acceptance.

attributes.text: Operator rulings 19 Aug 2026 (mobile, in-chat): (1) payments must be an international Merchant of Record - Stripe rejected for this role; (2) Next.js excluded, want simpler/faster; (3) datastore chosen on problem fit not founder fluency; (4) AI-agent search/extract/digest of the data is a first-class stack criterion; (5) engine tolerance relative-with-floor; (6) prices are precision-preserving decimals with display transform (no 2-d.p. assumption); (7) survey sample-size adequacy is not the engine's problem (broker, not analyser).
